title: Feminist groups march in Sofia against violence toward women
seoTitle: Sofia march against violence toward women

tea.why: Protesters marched to demand an end to violence against women and to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded crisis centers in every region, legal and psychological aid, legal definitions of femicide, and school education.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Thousands marched in Sofia and other cities on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

summary: Hundreds of people gathered in central Sofia for a demonstration in support of women who have faced violence, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The event was organized by the Feminist Mobilizations collective and the LevFem group, with support from the Bulgarian Fund for Women. Demonstrators marched through major boulevards and squares, holding placards and chanting slogans. Similar protests took place in other Bulgarian cities including Plovdiv, Varna, Burgas, Veliko Tarnovo, Stara Zagora, Tryavna, and Sliven. Organisers called for the establishment of crisis counseling centers in every region, free legal and psychological assistance for victims, unified data collection, legislative amendments addressing femicide, and mandatory sex education in schools. The demands were submitted to members of Parliament with a deadline of December 10 for official responses.
demands: Establish crisis and counselling centres in every region
Ensure access to free legal and psychological assistance for victims
Introduce a unified official system for collecting data on violence against women
Legislative amendments addressing femicide and gender-based violence
Mandatory age-appropriate sex education in schools
response: No official response reported in the sources.
